title: Inefficient Rebuild: setState() called on every scroll event
problem: setState(() {}) is called on every scroll event in the scroll listener, which is very inefficient and causes constant widget rebuilds as the user scrolls.
impact: Performance degradation - excessive widget rebuilds during scrolling lead to UI jank and increased CPU usage, draining battery on mobile devices.
solution: Implement throttling or debouncing for the scroll listener to limit how often setState() is called. Consider using a Timer to delay setState() calls or only update when scroll position crosses meaningful thresholds.

title: Inefficient Rebuild: Multiple FutureBuilders causing frequent rebuilds
problem: Multiple FutureBuilder widgets are rebuilt frequently, causing unnecessary widget tree reconstructions. The FutureBuilders reload data on every build cycle.
impact: Unnecessary widget tree reconstructions and data reloading on every build cycle, leading to performance issues and potential flickering.
solution: Consider caching the futures or combining data loading operations to reduce rebuilds. Cache Future results in State variables and reuse them across builds instead of creating new Futures in the build method.

title: Inefficient Rebuild: ValueKey causing unnecessary rebuilds
problem: ValueKey using ConfigParam.fontSize.val() will cause unnecessary rebuilds when the font size value changes.
impact: Unnecessary widget recreation when font size changes, even when the widget content hasn't meaningfully changed.
solution: Review the key generation strategy to avoid unnecessary widget recreation. Consider using a more stable key or implementing shouldRebuild logic to determine if the widget actually needs to be recreated.
